title: The Letter to the Ephesians Timeline
sub: Chosen and Sealed · One Body, Walking in Love and Light
desc: A letter that opens in one long sentence of blessing, moving from being dead in sin to being seated with Christ in the heavenly places, before turning practical, one body built up by gifted leaders, a household transformed by Christlike love, and a closing call to put on the full armor of God.

eras.label: Era One · Ephesians 1
eras.name: Chosen and Sealed — Every Spiritual Blessing
eras.dates: A single long sentence of blessing opens the letter, tracing salvation from before creation to a Spirit-sealed inheritance

events.title: Greeting, Then Blessed With Every Spiritual Blessing
events.detail: One unbroken sentence in the original Greek sweeps from election before creation, through redemption in Christ's blood, to being sealed with the promised Holy Spirit as a down payment on a coming inheritance.

verses.text: “He chose us in Him before the foundation of the world, that we would be holy and blameless before Him in love, by predestining us to adoption as sons.”
“You were sealed in Him with the Holy Spirit of promise, who is given as a pledge of our inheritance.”

events.title: A Prayer for the Spirit of Wisdom and Revelation
events.detail: Paul prays that the Ephesians would grasp the scale of what they've received: the same power that raised Christ from the dead and seated him far above every rule and authority now works toward those who believe.

verses.text: “The surpassing greatness of His power toward us who believe… which He worked in Christ, by raising Him from the dead and seating Him at His right hand in the heavenly places.”

eras.label: Era Two · Ephesians 2
eras.name: By Grace You Have Been Saved
eras.dates: Dead, then made alive; divided, then made one: two resurrections in a single chapter

events.title: Dead in Trespasses, Made Alive by Grace
events.detail: The letter's most quoted statement of salvation: once dead in sin and following the world's course, believers are made alive together with Christ purely by grace through faith, not by works, so no one can boast.

verses.text: “By grace you have been saved through faith, and this not of yourselves, it is the gift of God; not of works, so that no one may boast.”
“We are His workmanship, created in Christ Jesus for good works, which God prepared beforehand so that we would walk in them.”

events.title: One New Humanity: The Dividing Wall Broken Down
events.detail: Gentiles once excluded from Israel's covenants are now brought near through Christ's blood, who himself dissolves the hostility between Jew and Gentile and builds both into one temple with the apostles and prophets as its foundation.

verses.text: “He Himself is our peace, who made both groups one and broke down the dividing wall of the partition.”
“You are fellow citizens with the saints, and are of God's household, having been built on the foundation of the apostles and prophets, Christ Jesus Himself being the corner stone.”

eras.label: Era Three · Ephesians 3
eras.name: The Mystery Revealed to the Gentiles
eras.dates: A prisoner's parenthesis on his own calling, ending in one of Paul's grandest doxologies

events.title: Paul's Stewardship of a Long-Hidden Mystery
events.detail: Paul explains his specific calling as steward of a mystery hidden for ages: that Gentiles are now full co-heirs with Israel in the same body and promise: a mystery he calls himself the very least of all saints to proclaim.

verses.text: “The Gentiles are fellow heirs and fellow members of the body, and fellow partakers of the promise in Christ Jesus through the gospel.”

events.title: A Prayer to Comprehend the Breadth of Christ's Love
events.detail: Paul kneels in prayer for inner strength, for Christ to dwell in their hearts through faith, and for the ability to grasp a love that, by his own admission, surpasses knowledge altogether.

verses.text: “May be able to comprehend with all the saints what is the breadth and length and height and depth, and to know the love of Christ which surpasses knowledge.”

events.title: Far More Abundantly Beyond All We Ask
events.detail: A short, soaring doxology closes the doctrinal half of the letter, praising the God whose power works within believers to do more than they could ever ask or imagine.

verses.text: “Now to Him who is able to do far more abundantly beyond all that we ask or understand, according to the power that works within us, to Him be the glory… to all generations forever and ever.”

eras.label: Era Four · Ephesians 4
eras.name: One Body, Grow Up Into Christ
eras.dates: The letter turns from doctrine to practice, one body given gifted leaders so it can grow into maturity together

events.title: Walk Worthy: One Body, One Spirit, One Lord
events.detail: Paul, again naming himself a prisoner, calls for humility and patience in keeping a unity that already exists, stacking seven 'ones' that describe a church already unified before it's ever told to act like it.

verses.text: “There is one body and one Spirit… one Lord, one faith, one baptism; one God and Father of all who is over all and through all and in all.”

events.title: Gifts Given to Equip the Saints for Growth
events.detail: Christ's ascent is pictured as a conquering king distributing spoils (apostles, prophets, evangelists, pastors, and teachers) given not to do all the church's work themselves but to equip everyone else for it, until the body matures.

verses.text: “For the equipping of the saints for the work of service, to the building up of the body of Christ, until we all attain to the unity of the faith… to a mature man.”

events.title: Put Off the Old Self, Put On the New
events.detail: A detailed contrast between the futile, darkened life the Ephesians left behind and the new self created in true righteousness: worked out in concrete instructions about lying, anger, theft, and speech.

verses.text: “Put on the new man, which in the likeness of God has been created in righteousness and holiness of the truth.”
“Be kind to one another, tender-hearted, graciously forgiving each other, just as God in Christ also has graciously forgiven you.”

eras.label: Era Five · Ephesians 5
eras.name: Walk in Love, Walk in Light
eras.dates: Imitation of God, then a household code built around the deepest comparison Paul ever draws between marriage and the gospel

events.title: Children of Light: Walk in Love, Expose the Darkness
events.detail: Believers are told to imitate God as beloved children, avoiding the sins that provoke his wrath, and to live as light exposing the unfruitful works of darkness rather than participating in them.

verses.text: “You were formerly darkness, but now you are light in the Lord; walk as children of light.”

events.title: Be Filled With the Spirit, Not With Wine
events.detail: A call to redeem the time in an evil age, contrasting drunken dissipation with Spirit-filled worship, singing, thanksgiving, and mutual submission out of reverence for Christ.

verses.text: “Do not get drunk with wine, for that is dissipation, but be filled with the Spirit.”

events.title: Wives, Husbands, and the Marriage That Pictures Christ and the Church
events.detail: The longest household-code passage in Paul's letters explicitly ties marriage to the gospel itself: husbands are told to love their wives with the same self-giving love Christ showed the church, calling the whole comparison a great mystery.

verses.text: “Husbands, love your wives, just as Christ also loved the church and gave Himself up for her.”
“The two shall become one flesh. This mystery is great, but I am speaking with reference to Christ and the church.”

eras.label: Era Six · Ephesians 6
eras.name: The Armor of God
eras.dates: The household code's final pairs, then a closing image of spiritual warfare that has outlasted every other passage in the letter

events.title: Children, Fathers, Slaves, and Masters
events.detail: The household code concludes with children and fathers, then slaves and masters, both parties reminded that their real Master is in heaven, and that he shows no partiality between slave and free.

verses.text: “Masters, do the same things to them, giving up threatening, knowing that both their Master and yours is in heaven, and there is no partiality with Him.”

events.title: The Full Armor of God
events.detail: The letter's most famous image: a struggle not against flesh and blood but against spiritual authorities, met piece by piece with truth, righteousness, the gospel of peace, faith, salvation, the Spirit's sword, and constant prayer.

verses.text: “Our struggle is not against flesh and blood, but against the rulers, against the authorities, against the world forces of this darkness, against the spiritual forces of wickedness in the heavenly places.”
“Take up the full armor of God, so that you will be able to resist in the evil day, and having done everything, to stand firm.”

events.title: Closing: Tychicus Sent to Encourage Them
events.detail: Paul sends Tychicus to report on his own circumstances as a prisoner and to encourage the Ephesians' hearts, closing the letter with a benediction of peace, love, faith, and grace.

verses.text: “Grace be with all those who love our Lord Jesus Christ with incorruptible love.”
